text:
You need a native mobile solution for real-time object detection that can use the camera feed to recognize objects accurately and run reliably in a production app.

I’m Noor Halden, and I have 6 years of experience building machine learning and Python-based solutions with PyTorch, scikit-learn, LangChain, OpenAI API, Hugging Face Transformers, NLP, XGBoost, pandas, and machine learning workflows. While my background is centered on ML development rather than native mobile app implementation alone, I’ve built camera-based detection systems and deployed them in production settings, which aligns closely with the core of your project.

One relevant project was Ceramic tile defect detection for Halvorsen Ceramics. I built a camera-based crack and chip detector using Python, PyTorch, YOLOv8, OpenCV, and ONNX, then exported it for deployment on an industrial PC beside the kiln line. The system achieved 97.4% recall on cracks and reduced false rejects from 8% to 2.1%. That project required practical computer vision work, model optimization, and deployment-oriented thinking for a real production environment.

For your job, I can help design and develop the object detection pipeline, train and fine-tune the model, and focus on making it fast and dependable for live camera input. I’m comfortable working with clean, readable, well-documented code and with iterating on model performance based on real-world evaluation. I also understand how important it is to keep the implementation practical so it can be integrated into a mobile app workflow.

If helpful, I can also prepare an example of real-time object detection by camera as requested, and discuss how the model can be structured for integration into your iOS/Android product. I’m used to explaining technical decisions clearly and working through complex ML problems in a collaborative environment.

If you’re looking for someone who can bring strong ML and computer vision experience to a real-time detection feature, I’d be glad to help.
